status: WIP: live-reader semantic and construction checks complete; initial eight-client regression not consistently reproduced; no stable broad gain claimed

change.mechanism: Replace eager copies of eight expression globals with a live reader capturing the statement-selected GlobalSysvars owner. Clones retain that owner without copying values; peer updates are visible at evaluation, while scratch validation contexts stay isolated. Move the existing global-scope check to the owning table and use it from both session reads and callbacks. Remove the old snapshot builder and map field.
change.scope: No shared live password settings changed. No session-generation cache, dictionary copy, workload-specific branch or new reverse dependency.

regression.red: Old context returns Int(0) after peer enables validation; expected Int(100).
regression.coverage: Actual builtin evaluation through query, DML and cloned contexts; live peer mutations; scratch owner selected at construction, retained after restoring the live table, and observing its own later changes.

construction_benchmark.interpretation: Five samples per dictionary size and context class, 10000 constructions/drops per sample after 100 warmups. Same benchmark source before/after implementation; no simultaneous build, profiling or SQL load during timing. Independent before/after test binaries; not paired interleaving, so host drift limits precision. Empty-catalog statement setup only, not SQL throughput. Dictionary-size scaling disappears without evaluating a password builtin; no timing assertion.

profiling.scope: Eight-client full TPC-C mix, 20000 transactions per release, sequential; excluded from throughput measurement.
profiling.method: macOS sample, 15 seconds at 1ms; llvm-cxxfilt demangling and heuristic wait-leaf subtraction. Inclusive counts overlap and are not CPU-time percentages.
profiling.finding: No obvious new global-reader lock hotspot. Optimizer cost parsing is still entered on ordinary statements. Source trace finds unconditional variable-generation bump on empty SET_VAR restoration, invalidating existing caches; investigate as a separate root optimization, not as a proven cause of the initial slowdown.
